In mathematics, especially [[algebraic geometry]] and [[algebraic topology]], a '''higher stack''' is a [[higher category]] generalization of a [[stack (mathematics)|stack]] (a category-valued sheaf). The notion goes back to Grothendieck’s ''[[Pursuing Stacks]]''.<ref>{{harvnb|Töen|2014|loc=§ 1. Selected pieces of history.}}</ref>

Toën suggests the following principle:<ref>Bertrand Toën, Higher and Derived Stacks: A Global Overview, arXiv:math /0604504</ref>
{{blockquote|As 1-stacks appear as soon as objects must be classified up to isomorphism, higher stacks appear as soon as objects must be classified up to a notion of equivalence which is weaker than the notion of isomorphism.}}

Sometimes a [[derived stack]] (or a [[spectral stack]]) is defined as a higher stack of some sort.
